Database Transaction Isolation Levels Reference Guide

Transactions in relational database systems are governed by ACID properties. Isolation is the 'I' in ACID, defining how transaction integrity is visible to other concurrent operations. SQL-92 defines four standard isolation levels to manage three read phenomena: dirty reads, non-repeatable reads, and phantom reads. Higher isolation levels prevent more phenomena but reduce concurrent performance due to locking overhead.

Read Committed is the default isolation level in PostgreSQL and SQL Server. In Read Committed, a query within a transaction only sees data committed before the query began, not before the transaction began. This prevents Dirty Reads, where a transaction reads uncommitted changes from another. However, Non-Repeatable Reads can still occur. This happens if another transaction commits changes between two executions of the same query within the first transaction, resulting in different data returned.

Repeatable Read isolation level guarantees that any data read during a transaction will remain consistent throughout its duration. In PostgreSQL, this level prevents both Dirty Reads and Non-Repeatable Reads. It also prevents Phantom Reads, where concurrent transactions insert new rows that would match a search criteria. If a concurrent transaction modifies data that a Repeatable Read transaction attempts to update, PostgreSQL throws a serialization failure error, forcing the application to retry.

Serializable is the highest isolation level. It guarantees strict physical serializability, meaning the concurrent execution of transactions produces the exact same state as if they were run one after another sequentially. Serializable isolation uses lock-free Serializable Snapshot Isolation (SSI) in PostgreSQL to detect read-write conflicts. If a conflict occurs, one of the transactions is terminated with a 40001 serialization failure code. While it guarantees absolute data consistency, it carries the highest application overhead due to transaction retry requirements.
